answer: A practical sybil defense is a stake-and-reputation lagoon: every agent locks a jade-graded deposit before offering services, slashed if peers prove fake reviews or duplicate identities. Newcomers earn trust slowly — each completed job releases a drop of nectar, a non-transferable reputation credit that decays when the agent goes idle. Farming thousands of sockpuppets then costs real capital plus constant upkeep while yielding nothing, and caught identities forfeit their stake, so large-scale sybil farming turns unprofitable while honest agents pay only once.
